$comment: Module batch 3 (home) — the five S/home cells with no board. GROUP ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: /wallet runs FIRST because /parallel arms a PERSISTED flag, and the two cold-wallet boards are the only ones that need a browser which has never seen it. Run the file whole; --group /parallel alone is safe, --group /wallet alone is only safe in a fresh profile (which is what the driver always gives it).

states.note: the hero before any balance is known: BalanceSkeleton (HomeScreen.tsx:104-105, gated by balanceUnknown at useHomeController.ts:188) in place of the figure — the app's answer to 'not known yet', which a rebuilder would otherwise draw as a fake $0.00
states.$why: forbidRe is the real assertion: EVERY other Home board shows either a resolved figure or the six privacy dots, so 'no $ figure anywhere' is a post-condition none of them satisfies. Verified in the dump: a 208x46 #F5F3EF radius-8 bar at (24,108.5) where the amount goes.
states.$mechanism: This profile has no wallet at all (localStorage is empty, measured), so `address` is undefined, loadData never runs and balanceUnknown stays true indefinitely — the skeleton is still on screen at 65 s. That makes the state stable to capture instead of a race, and the PICTURE is the same one a real first load shows; only the header identity differs (monogram 'W' / name 'Wallet' rather than a real account).

states.note: HoldingsList's empty-wallet card (HoldingsList.tsx:144-153) — accent ArrowDown medallion over 'Deposit your first asset', the whole card a Pressable routing to /receive. NOT the filtered-empty branch (:141-143), which is a bare 'No matching tokens' line.
states.$why: differsFrom home-balance-loading is the one that matters: a silently-missed 'Assets' click (the react-navigation ghost bug) reproduces exactly the state captured immediately before this one. forbid 'No activity yet' catches the same failure from the text side, and forbidRe catches the empty card being drawn over a funded holdings list ($2.26 / $1.00 / $0.02 on the populated Assets tab).
states.$note-on-differsFrom: S/home/assets is deliberately NOT a differsFrom target: run-capture's findDump resolves the slug 'home-assets' to dom-dumps/pruned/home-assets.json (an older generation) before it ever reaches dom-dumps/screens, so the check would silently compare against the wrong picture. `expect` covers that confusion instead — the populated board cannot contain 'Deposit your first asset'.
expect: Tap here to see your address

$order: default → refreshing → estimate-notice. The fault board is LAST because an injected fault survives to the end of the group (capture-states.js clears it there), and because home-refreshing needs an unfaulted at-rest sibling — home-default — to be asserted against.

states.note: the POPULATED activity feed — day header plus one ActivityRow (direction, counterparty alias, +amount, fiat subline). The only board anywhere in the file that shows an ActivityRow in context.
states.$why: The fixture Safe has no transaction history and no vela.* command seeds one, so the feed is reached through useHomeController's own dev seam (:238-257), which is a bare global rather than a vela.* member — hence the `call` act. The receipt TOAST covers the row for 2.8 s (:233), so the dwell is 3.5 s and `forbid: USDC received` proves it has cleared: that string exists only in the toast (home.toastReceived = '{{amount}} {{token}} received'), never in the row, whose parts render as 'Received' + '+12.5 USDC' on separate lines.
states.$why-the-tab-bounce: THE SIMULATED ROW HAS A 10-SECOND LIFETIME AND THE CLOCK IS NOT YOURS. useHomeController.ts:379-384 runs loadData() on a 10 s interval while the Activity tab is open, and loadData's first step calls commitActivity(items) unconditionally (:275) with the PERSISTED feed — which does not contain the simulated item. Measured: with no bounce the row survived 1.5 s, 8.1 s and 8.1 s on three consecutive tries (the wipes land exactly 10 s apart — you inherit whatever phase the page booted with, so this recipe passes about half the time and its first full-file run failed on 'Today'). That effect's deps are [tab, loadData], so leaving Activity CLEARS the interval and returning re-arms a fresh one: after the bounce the row survived 10.1 s on three of three tries. The capture lands ~4.2 s after the call, i.e. ~5.8 s of headroom. Do not remove the bounce, and do not lengthen the dwell past ~7 s.

states.note: VelaRefresh held open while loadData runs: the branded arc indicator spinning over the 'Updated now' freshness caption, the whole feed translated 72 px (VelaRefresh REST = TRIGGER = 72) down the screen
states.$why: slowRpc turns a 300 ms animation frame into a several-second resting state: `refreshing` stays true for the whole of loadData and VelaRefresh springs pull to REST and holds it (VelaRefresh.tsx:126-131), so the capture is not a race. It is also what makes differsFrom airtight — every way the pull can fail (no touch, under-threshold, busy) skips loadData, which means the simulated ActivityRow from home-default is NOT wiped and the picture is byte-for-byte home-default. Measured on the dump: 'Total balance · USD' moves y=80 → y=152, the tab row 204.5 → 276.5, the 'Updated now' caption is exposed at y=119.5, and an arc indicator appears at ~(175,77) — 32x32 in one run, 42x42 in another because it is mid-spin — a node neither sibling has at all.

states.note: the hero's approximation row — amber AlertTriangle, the sentence, ChevronRight into BalanceDetailSheet (HomeScreen.tsx:110-129) — sitting over the SURVIVING cached total with NO RpcTroubleBanner. The banner suppression is the point (HomeScreen.tsx:133-139).
states.$why: nullPrice(56) leaves the fixture's BNB held but unpriced → hasUnpriced → balancePartial, while failedChainIds stays empty → no banner, and displayTotal falls back to max(live, cached) so the $3.2x survives. The notice is NOT immediate: three silent force-retries (1.5 s + 4 s + 8 s, useHomeController.ts:53-54, :352-366) must exhaust before noticeAllowed flips. Measured from the pull: 12.9 s in one run, under 3 s in another (the retry budget carries over) — so the dwell is 16 s and a second pull + 12 s is the belt-and-braces. Do NOT use rateLimitRpc('all') here: state-specs-5.json's recipe does, and it writes $0.00 over the cached total with neither notice nor banner.
states.$why-the-12s-drain: the previous state armed slowRpc, and VelaRefresh REFUSES a new pull while its own refresh is in flight (`if (busy.value ...) return`, VelaRefresh.tsx:167). Clearing the fault does not cancel the sleeps already started, so this state waits the slow refresh out before pulling — otherwise the pull is silently swallowed and the fault never reaches a fetch.
